row.evidence: cyberark.com/pricing now redirects to the Idira (Palo Alto Networks) platform page with only demo/contact options, while Idira Identity docs describe an inbound SCIM server that "provisions users and groups to Idira Identity from other applications".
row.notes: Quote-only: CyberArk was rebranded as Idira by Palo Alto Networks; cyberark.com/pricing redirects to paloaltonetworks.com/idira, which lists no plans or prices, so the inbound SCIM server (part of Idira Identity, formerly CyberArk Identity) can only be bought through sales. Scored as a provisioning target: Idira Identity runs a SCIM 2.0 server (Users, Groups plus PAM objects for Privilege Cloud) authenticated with an OAuth2 client-credentials bearer token; endpoints manage Cloud Directory ('Vault') users only. Idira Identity is itself an IdP with outbound SCIM to apps (other_sync). Research covered the Identity Administration service; Privilege Cloud / PAM consume these users.

auth.token_source: Admin Portal > Web Apps > Add Web Apps > Custom > OAuth2 client (Client Creds, scope REST regex scim*); Actions > Create Bearer Token

deprovision.notes: An 'active' boolean is in the supported core attributes and filterable, but the docs do not describe active=false as a deactivation flow.

limitations.text: SCIM endpoints manage Cloud Directory (Vault) users only, not AD, LDAP, Azure AD or Google-connected directory users.

endpoints.purpose: Create a Cloud Directory user (method not shown on page; Identity platform calls are POST)
Lock, disable, expire or re-enable (None) a user
Create a role and add members

okta.notes: OIN listing exists but marks no capabilities in the page markup.

entra.notes: CyberArk SAML Authentication gallery app (SSO tutorial; no provisioning tutorial found).

fallbacks.other_sync: Idira Identity is itself an IdP with outbound SCIM provisioning to external apps
